First time here! And, I have to admit that as a movie buff, I had never actually seen this one before, and was not familiar with the characters that the director put us through here. What was nice was that as I sat and watched, I was able to immerse myself in the movie, and even as I watched many of the characters, I ended up feeling more connected to them as time passed and I learned more about their back stories and motivations. The two most prominent characters in this story are Harry, a former detective, who gets a call to come in to help his son, who accidentally stabs his girlfriend just before she is about to give birth. Harry had been trying to build a relationship with his son, and after her death, thought that he should let him take the wheel. The boy wanted to be a cop, and after he left home for the first time, Harry followed in his car. He ends up getting lost and finds a motel where he meets his son, who has run away from home. It's an eerie coincidence that his son ends up back in the motel and Harry is able to talk with him - not a detail that Harry would like for the kid to know, as he's hoping to give him up to his parents, but in an unfortunate way this makes them a lot like siblings. Once he learns who's in there with him - her husband, played by Kevin Connolly - Harry does what a man should: stand up to him and try to talk him down. As a policeman, he used to work with his wife, and Harry can see that her death changed him, turning him into someone who wants revenge. Meanwhile, the older boy is the one who is most affected by what happened to his mother. It was his girlfriend, played by Sarah Drew, who stabbed her, but this scene alone sets the scene for the rest of the movie! In the motel one night, Harry ends up accidentally awakening the older boy and finds he's actually his son, though he doesn't remember him at first. Things start to get strange, and Harry soon learns that he can't get rid of this guy in his own town, so he sends him back to his father's home, in a family far from the life he left behind. It's not long before the boy starts to turn more and more toward Harry, and Harry needs to be sure about how much he's willing to take on before he takes on his father. The reason I'm mentioning the story here is that the biggest problem I think is that a lot of the story is focused on Harry, and the younger boy, but the dialogue between them is pretty weak. There are moments where it feels like they're trying to talk each other out, but they don't really seem to have anything to say, and they don't give the viewer much direction as to what they're feeling. Maybe that's good? Maybe the director is trying to take us into the hearts of the characters, but at times it's hard to find. The acting is great in general, however, as every actor nails the part they're playing, it just feels like the screenplay doesn't really pick up until the end where the plot is forced to a certain conclusion. Still, this is a story that's worth seeing, even if it doesn't do much for me personally. Overall, not too bad! It definitely has it's weak points, but the plot is decent and there are interesting characters in it. Definitely check it out if you get the chance.
